articles.title: Claude Code vs Codex CLI: 18 Commands and Flags Side by Side
articles.excerpt: Book: AI Agents Pocket Guide Also by me: Thinking in Go (2-book series) — Complete Guide to Go Programming + Hexagonal Architecture in Go My project: Hermes IDE | GitHub — an IDE for developers who sh…
articles.body: Book: AI Agents Pocket Guide Also by me: Thinking in Go (2-book series) — Complete Guide to Go Programming + Hexagonal Architecture in Go My project: Hermes IDE | GitHub — an IDE for developers who ship with Claude Code and other AI coding tools Me: xgabriel.com | GitHub In Claude Code , -p means print: run the prompt, write the answer, exit. In Codex CLI , -p is --profile , so codex -p "fix the flaky test" asks for a config profile with that name. -c continues your last conversation in Claude Code. In Codex it sets a config key. If you run both agents every day, your fingers will pick the wrong one sooner or later. So here are 18 tasks, the Claude Code way and the Codex way, each with a command you can paste.

articles.title: Parallel Coding Agents Leave 9 Kinds of Junk on Your Disk. The Commands That Clear It
articles.excerpt: Book: AI That Acts The series: AI in TypeScript — 5 books, from your first LLM call to agents in production — all five here My project: Hermes IDE | GitHub — an IDE for developers who ship with Claude…
articles.body: Book: AI That Acts The series: AI in TypeScript — 5 books, from your first LLM call to agents in production — all five here My project: Hermes IDE | GitHub — an IDE for developers who ship with Claude Code and other AI coding tools Me: xgabriel.com | GitHub Codex keeps the 15 most recent worktrees it manages by default, and deletes older ones to stay under that limit or when you archive a chat. Claude Code removes a clean worktree automatically when you exit an unnamed interactive session; a named one asks first. A claude -p --worktree run has no exit prompt, so its worktree stays on disk, still locked until a later session's sweep releases it. Add the worktrees you made by hand for a third agent, and a few weeks of parallel work leaves a lot behind.

articles.title: Astronomers discover the 1st ever green star, a cosmic zombie just in time for Halloween
articles.excerpt: Imagine if the sun could take on a spooky green glow for Halloween. Scientists have discovered that our star may go green if it turns into a cosmic zombie after its death in billions of years.
articles.body: How awesome would it be if the sun could take on a spooky green glow for Halloween? It turns out that scientists have discovered that our star may indeed go green, but only billions of years from now after its death — and only if it then starts eating planets like a cosmic zombie. That's possible because scientists have discovered that white dwarfs, the type of stellar remnants sun-sized stars leave behind when they die, can actually take on a range of colors including green if they snack on their rocky planets like cosmic cannibals. For stellar scientists, the colors of stars have always been indicative of their temperatures. Cool stars look orange, while stars like the sun look white , and the hottest stars glow pale blue.

articles.title: /compact or /compress? 9 Agent Commands in Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and OpenCode
articles.excerpt: Book: Observability for LLM Applications Also by me: Thinking in Go (2-book series) — Complete Guide to Go Programming + Hexagonal Architecture in Go My project: Hermes IDE | GitHub — an IDE for devel…
articles.body: Book: Observability for LLM Applications Also by me: Thinking in Go (2-book series) — Complete Guide to Go Programming + Hexagonal Architecture in Go My project: Hermes IDE | GitHub — an IDE for developers who ship with Claude Code and other AI coding tools Me: xgabriel.com | GitHub Your Gemini CLI session is getting long, so you type /compact . Gemini CLI has no /compact . Its command is /compress , and the docs describe it in one line: "Replace the entire chat context with a summary." Claude Code , Codex CLI and OpenCode all call it /compact . That's one mismatch. articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 15, 1997: NASA launches Cassini-Hugyens probe on 7-year voyage to Saturn
articles.excerpt: On this day in space! Oct. 15, 1997: NASA launches Cassini-Hugyens probe on 7-year voyage to Saturn
articles.body: On Oct. 15, 1997, NASA launched the Cassini spacecraft on a mission to explore Saturn and its moons. It lifted off aboard a Titan 4B rocket from Cape Canaveral Air Force Station in Florida. It took almost seven years for the Cassini spacecraft to reach Saturn , with the spacecraft entering orbit around the ringed planet in 2004. Another smaller spacecraft called Huygens hitched a ride with Cassini, and it landed on Saturn's moon Titan in 2005. Cassini spent 13 years studying the Saturn system up close, and the mission lasted about 20 years before coming to an epic grand finale on Sept. 15, 2017 . articles.title: The 9 Biggest RPG Jerk Companions, Ranked From Worst to Even Worse

articles.body: You rolled your eyes at their first line, considered leaving them at camp, and now you can’t imagine the party without them. Every RPG has one: the companion whose first impression is a red flag, and whose second, third, and fiftieth impressions are the reason you keep playing. Often, you’ll find that even the most gruff or off-putting companion has a heart of gold somewhere deep down. Sometimes very deep down, but still. You might realize that a krogan mercenary’s temper comes from a plague that is killing off his whole race. (Or you might just decide to kill these brusque companion candidates on sight and call it a day.) These nine companions, ranked from merely irritating to the worst of the bunch, are your field guides to the red flags that you might, with time, learn to ignore.

Dynamic Aviation Agricultural emissions represent an important and understudied part of Earth’s land and atmosphere systems.
